incident-bot: ALERT: service:hosted-inference errors > 5% for 5m in us-east-1, paging oncall (pagerduty: P12345) :rotating_light:
Samir K.: seeing 502s on /v1/generate and elevated latency, pulling logs now. Oncall switching to me.
Mia A.: thx Samir — hey CS, seeing customer-facing errors? I can start drafting a status page message.
Elaine R.: we already got 3 CS tickets about failed completions from BrightApps and Acme. Both on Dedicated but routed through hosted fallback. Customers asking for ETA.
Samir K.: mitigation steps: 1) scale up pool-hosted-1 by +2 instances (in progress) 2) route traffic for dedicated->fallback-disabled for afflicted customers to their dedicated pools (manual) 3) enable short-term 0.5s prefix cache bypass.
Carla J. (SRE): creating failover route now. logs show spike in model kernel OOMs around 2026-02-18T03:21Z. pushing config change to reduce max_seq_length to 1024 for older model variants as temporary workaround.
Samir K.: updated status: added 2 instances, failover route applied for Acme, BrightApps still pending verification. Error rate trending down from 8% -> 3% in the last 12m.
Mia A.: draft status page blurb: "We are investigating elevated 502/timeout errors impacting inference requests in us-east-1. Some Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput. Engineers are applying scaling and routing workarounds; mitigation in progress. No data loss suspected. We will provide updates in 30 minutes." Thoughts?
Elaine R.: tweak: call out affected surface: "text generation and chat endpoints (generation, chat completions)." Also add customer contact path: support@redwood.com and their account manager name.
Mia A.: updated: "We are investigating elevated 502/timeout errors impacting text generation and chat endpoints in us-east-1. Some Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput; engineers are applying scaling and routing workarounds. No data loss suspected. If you're affected contact support@redwood.com or your account manager. Next update in 30 minutes." Ready to publish? :eyes:
Samir K.: go ahead. I'll mark when we've stabilized.
incident-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATE: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260218-01 posted by Mia A.
Elaine R.: sent customer notification to BrightApps (copy below) — pinging for ack from Samir before I send to Acme:
Elaine R.: "Hi BrightApps team — we observed increased 502/timeout errors for inference requests affecting some of your traffic routed through our us-east-1 cluster. Our engineers implemented scaling and routing mitigations; you may see intermittent retries while we validate recovery. Estimated time to stable: 20–40 minutes. If you need a private incident call, ping me. Sorry for the disruption — Elaine, Customer Success."
Samir K.: ack on BrightApps note. For Acme, please add: mention their dedicated pool was routed to fallback and we reverted when we confirmed capacity. Also offer a short credits gesture if they had >5% failed requests during the window.
Elaine R.: noted. Draft for Acme: "Hi Acme team — during the incident Acme's dedicated pool briefly routed to hosted fallback causing higher latency and some failures. We reverted routing and scaled capacity; mitigation completed at 2026-02-18T03:41Z. We're offering a service credit for impacted requests. I'll follow up with a short timeline and RCA once available. — Elaine, CS"
Mia A.: adding action item: "CS to send customer-specific timelines + credit offer; Eng to publish RCA draft and timeline; SRE to confirm final root cause and permanent fix ETA."
Carla J. (SRE): preliminary notes for RCA timeline (for CS): "03:18Z - increased OOMs on model-worker nodes; 03:20Z - error rate spike detected and alerted; 03:23Z - autoscaler lagged due to throttled API calls; 03:27Z - manual scale +2 applied; 03:31Z - failover routing applied for Acme; 03:41Z - error rate < 0.5% and validation checks green."
Raj P.: can we provide the exact query count impacted so CS can quantify the credit? I can run a query against request logs and produce counts by tenant for the 03:15-03:45 window.
Samir K.: please do, Raj. prioritize Acme and BrightApps.
Raj P.: running now — provisional totals: BrightApps 1,420 failed requests; Acme 3,210 failed requests; other tenants combined ~980. I'll attach CSV to the RCA doc.
Elaine R.: perfect. I'll send Acme draft with numbers and the credit formula: 1 free hour of dedicated capacity for failure rate >5% during window or a prorated credit equal to X% of billed usage for that hour.
Mia A.: also prepping internal post-incident comms for execs and ops: short summary, customer impact (tenants and counts), mitigation steps taken, and next steps (longer term autoscaler fix, kernel memory guarding, improved early OOM detection). Draft below:
Mia A.: "Executive summary: Brief spike in inference errors in us-east-1 due to model-worker OOMs and autoscaler throttling caused a 8% peak error rate; key customers Acme and BrightApps experienced increased failures. Mitigation completed within ~23 minutes via manual scaling and routing. No customer data was exposed. Next steps: patch autoscaler retry/backoff, kernel memory cap heuristic, and add tenant-level quick route actions in Console. RCA doc: link to follow."
Carla J. (SRE): adding technical next steps: "add guardrails in runtime to detect steady memory growth and proactively spin new warm workers when per-worker mem > 85% for 2 consecutive mins; tune autoscaler API rate limits; add a fallback traffic drain metric to Console for faster manual routing."
Elaine R.: sending final customer emails now. Will post final follow-up here with customer responses.
Samir K.: closing note for handoff: oncall will stay monitoring for 2 hours, Samir replicating memory heap traces to S3 for deeper debug. If CS wants to escalate to execs, ping me and I'll summarize.
Mia A.: thanks team — please add any missing timeline items below. We'll convert this thread into a short CS post-incident template and attach RCA link when ready. :white_check_mark:
